title: Banane malaxée (Topsi Banana)
author: Restaurant le Mvimli Bekot, Mbalmayo (camer.be)
desc: A restaurant’s large-batch mashed green banana with peanuts and smoked fish, cooked about 40 minutes in red palm oil and served lukewarm or cold.
longDesc: A restaurant’s printing on camer.be for 5 kg of green bananas. The bananas are peeled (the page says it is tedious since they are unripe; slitting the skin and rubbing with salt or red oil keeps the sap off the hands). The peanuts are sorted (soaked, roasted or crushed directly), the fish is beheaded, detailed and split, and the ginger, garlic, onion and pepper blended. The pot is filled to about three-quarters and red oil is warmed slightly; the bananas, fish, peanuts and salt go in; water is added to cover the bananas; covered and cooked 40 minutes (20 on high, then medium). Served lukewarm or cold. The cooked meat and the blended aromatics never appear in the steps — a gap stated plainly.
steps: Peel the bananas. Slit the skin and rub with salt or red oil to keep the sap off your hands.
Sort the peanuts (soak, roast, or crush directly). Behead, detail and split the fish and rinse the smoked fish. Blend the ginger, garlic, onion and chilli.
Fill the pot to about three-quarters and warm the red oil slightly.
Add the bananas, fish, peanuts and salt and stir. Add water to cover the bananas.
Cover and cook 40 minutes — 20 on high heat, then on medium. Serve lukewarm or cold.
chefTips: The only printed cues are the times (20 high, then medium to 40 minutes).
The page’s tip for the hands: rub with salt or red oil.
The meat and the blended aromatics are listed but not placed in the steps.
commonMistakes: Leaving out the aromatics because the steps do not mention them.
Skipping the water to cover the bananas.
reheating: Served lukewarm or cold per the page.
healthBenefits: Green banana for slow starch; peanuts and smoked fish for protein and fat.
culturalNote: The page says the dish is originally from the West region of Cameroon. The byline is a restaurant (Restaurant le Mvimli Bekot in Mbalmayo), and the date is a Sunday publication in camer.be’s ‘recette du dimanche’ series.
sources: Title as printed: ‘La banane malaxée ou le Topsi Banana’. Byline as printed: ‘Restaurant le Mvimli Bekot à Mbalmayo’ (restaurant byline; flagged). ‘Dimanche 20 septembre 2020 09:40’. Yield not printed (servings 20 is a placeholder for a 5 kg batch). TWO-PASS.

STEPS MISSING, stated plainly: the cooked meat and the blended ginger/garlic/onion/chilli appear in the ingredient list and preparation but not in the cooking step. ‘Teinte’ peanuts are as printed. ABSENT: water quantity; spice sachet size.
